Ole Dyg Pedersen is a Danish medical professional who serves as a Chief Physician (Overlæge) at Zealand University Hospital (Sjællands Universitetshospital) [^src1]. He plays a significant leadership role in national clinical quality improvement efforts for cardiovascular health in Denmark, specifically concerning the treatment and monitoring of atrial fibrillation.

Pedersen is a key figure in the governance of the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK). He is documented as a member of the database's steering group, contributing to the oversight of the clinical registry that tracks the quality of care for atrial fibrillation patients across the country [^src1]. By the time of the 2024 annual report, his leadership role had expanded, and he is explicitly identified as the chairperson (forperson) for the database within the broader [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] initiative [^src2]. His continued involvement in the program's governance is further confirmed by his membership in the [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]], which emphasizes the multidisciplinary and cross-sectoral nature of the national quality development program [^src3].

Through these positions, Pedersen is involved in the strategic and clinical decision-making processes that shape national guidelines. His work supports the AFDK's transition from hospital-centered reporting to population-based quality measurements across Denmark's 21 healthcare clusters, addressing critical clinical challenges such as anticoagulation therapy, echocardiography, and structured patient education.
